brief.t: Started in Jaipur in 1996 by Sanjay Agarwal as AU Financiers, a vehicle-finance company; became a small finance bank in April 2017.
In August 2025 it became the first small finance bank to get RBI's in-principle approval to turn into a universal bank; the final licence was still pending in Oct 2026.
Led by founder and MD & CEO Sanjay Agarwal, re-appointed for three years from April 2026; former RBI Deputy Governor H.R. Khan is Chairman.
FY 2025-26 net profit rose 25% to ₹2,641 crore.
Q2 FY27 (Jul–Sep 2026) profit jumped 53% to ₹858 crore, with deposits up 28.6%.

timeline.t: Sanjay Agarwal founded AU Financiers in Jaipur.
Began operations as a small finance bank.
Fincare Small Finance Bank merged into AU, the first merger of two SFBs.
RBI gave in-principle approval to become a universal bank.
Bought naming rights to a Mumbai Metro station, 'AU Bank Bandra Colony'.

model.how: AU lends mainly to small businesses, vehicle buyers, home buyers and self-employed people in smaller towns, often at higher rates. It funds this with fast-growing retail deposits and earns a wide interest gap.
flow: Bank lends to vehicle buyers, MSMEs, home buyers
Earns a wide interest gap + fees

points: Small finance banks must give most loans to small borrowers and priority sectors; a universal bank has fewer such limits.
AU is the first SFB on the path to becoming a full universal bank.
Big theme for interviews: how small finance banks grow into mainstream banks.

frameworks.note: Framework views are analysis built from the verified facts on this page, not company statements.

glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs, provisions and taxes. The bank's final earnings.
glossary.Net Interest Income: Interest earned on loans minus interest paid on deposits. A bank's main earning.
glossary.Net interest margin: Net Interest Income as a % of the bank's interest-earning assets. Shows how profitable lending is.
glossary.Gross NPA: Non-Performing Asset: a loan not repaid for 90+ days. Gross NPA is the % of all loans that have gone bad.
glossary.Net NPA: Bad loans after subtracting the money already set aside (provisions) for them. Lower is better.
glossary.CASA ratio: Share of deposits in Current and Savings accounts. These pay little interest, so a higher CASA means cheaper funds.
glossary.Capital adequacy ratio: The bank's own capital compared with the risk in its loans. RBI requires a minimum; higher means safer.
glossary.Provisions: Money set aside from profit to cover loans that may not be repaid.
glossary.Deposits: Money customers keep with the bank in savings, current and fixed deposit accounts.
glossary.Advances: Loans given by the bank to customers and businesses.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.Treasury gains: Profit from buying and selling bonds and other investments. It can swing a lot each quarter.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year. Also called employee turnover.
glossary.RBI: Reserve Bank of India, which regulates all banks in India.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer: checking a customer's identity before opening an account.
glossary.MSME: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises: small businesses that banks lend to.
glossary.Cross-sell: Selling an extra product (like a credit card) to an existing customer.
glossary.Public sector bank: A bank where the Government of India owns the majority of shares.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.
glossary.Small finance bank: A bank licensed by RBI to serve small businesses, farmers and low-income customers, with rules on how much it must lend to them.
glossary.Universal bank: A full-service bank that can offer all banking products to all customers, like HDFC Bank or SBI.
glossary.Touchpoints: All places where customers can reach the bank: branches, banking outlets and service centres.

Role knowledge, the bank and HR questions

Finance.q: What changes when a small finance bank becomes a universal bank?
Finance.a: Fewer rules on whom it must lend to, bigger loan limits and more products, so it can compete directly with large private banks.
It lends to small businesses and vehicle buyers at higher rates; its NIM was 5.8% in Q2 FY27.

Marketing.q: How would you rebrand AU when the 'Small' tag goes?
Marketing.a: Keep the trust it built in small towns, while showing big-bank strength through city campaigns like the Mumbai Metro station.

Marketing.q: How would you raise AU's CASA ratio?
Marketing.a: Salary-account tie-ups, a strong app, and current accounts for small businesses it already lends to.

HR.q: AU has about 59,000 employees. How would you prepare them for the universal bank move?
HR.a: Training on new products and rules, clear career paths and communication about what changes.

Sales.q: Sell an AU fixed deposit to a retired teacher.
Sales.a: Ask about needs, then explain safety, interest rate, and deposit insurance simply, and close with a next step.

Operations.q: How would you integrate two banks' systems after a merger like Fincare?
Operations.a: Map processes, migrate data in phases, train staff and keep customers informed.

Joining during this change means learning how a bank scales up. I want to be part of that journey and contribute to [your role].

gd.t: Should small finance banks become universal banks?
gd.for: It lets them grow and compete with big banks.
gd.against: They may drift away from serving small borrowers.

gd.t: Can regional banks compete with national giants?
gd.for: AU grew from Rajasthan to 21 states.
gd.against: Big banks have lower funding costs and bigger brands.

avoid: Don't say AU is already a universal bank; it has in-principle approval, with the final licence pending.
Don't call it an NBFC; it has been a bank since 2017.
Don't confuse AU Small Finance Bank with AU Financiers (its old name) or other SFBs like Ujjivan.
